No child was born out of the said wedlock.
4. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately since April, 2017.
Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against petitioner no.1 (husband) and petitioner no. 2 (mother-in-law).

5. On 14.06.2022, parties arrived at a settlement before Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts,
Delhi and as per the said settlement, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 43,50,000/-
to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan,
permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.
The copy of the aforesaid settlement deed dated 14.06.2022 is on record (Annexure P-3).

6. In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by a decree of divorce dated 09.02.2023, passed by Shri Raj Kumar Tripathi, Judge, Family Court-I (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi (Annexure P-5).

10. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
